items.stem: Define the term 'mail merge'.
items.answer: Combining a master document with records from a data source to produce many personalised documents automatically.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: Combining a master document with records from a data source to produce many personalised documents automatically. [2]

items.stem: Explain two advantages of mail merge over writing letters individually.
items.answer: Hundreds of personalised letters are produced quickly from one master; fewer errors because data is copied automatically; easy to update and re-run; consistent layout.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain why the data source should be checked before a mail merge is run.
items.answer: Errors, missing values or duplicates in the data will appear in every affected letter, wasting paper/postage and looking unprofessional.
items.markingKey: 1 mark errors copied to output; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem: Priya is setting up a mail merge at Meridian Hospital in Nairobi to invite members to an event. Describe what is meant by the master document.
items.answer: Fixed text plus merge fields used for every output document.

items.stem: Summit Engineering in Manila sends a personalised letter to each of its 3000 customers every month. (a) Describe what is meant by the master document. (b) Explain one problem that could occur.

items.stem: Meridian Hospital in Santiago wants to send different offers to members and non-members. (a) Explain how a filter would be used in this mailing. (b) Write a conditional field that prints "Gold member" if Points is over 1000 and "Member" otherwise.
